sources.name: NASA POWER
sources.measures: Daily and long-term weather and climate: temperature, rainfall, humidity, wind, solar radiation, soil wetness and reference evapotranspiration.
sources.limitations: Model and satellite estimates for a large grid cell, not a weather station on the farm. Rainfall in thunderstorms can differ a lot over short distances. The last few days may be missing.

sources.name: NASA SRTM elevation
sources.measures: Ground elevation, from which slope, low spots and erosion rating are worked out.
sources.limitations: Measured in 2000; does not see tile drains, small ditches or recent land levelling.

sources.name: NASA MODIS
sources.measures: Vegetation greenness (NDVI) every 16 days, yearly productivity and actual and potential evapotranspiration.
sources.limitations: A pixel can include neighbouring fields, trees or roads, so small fields are blended with their surroundings.

sources.name: NASA GRACE / GRACE-FO drought indicators
sources.provider: NASA and the National Drought Mitigation Center
sources.measures: Groundwater, root-zone and surface soil moisture as percentiles against past years, weekly.
sources.limitations: Regional; a single field's moisture can differ, especially with irrigation or drainage.

sources.name: Sentinel-2 (via NASA HLS)
sources.resolution: 10-30 m, every few days when not cloudy.
sources.limitations: Clouds, haze and snow block or distort observations, so there can be gaps of weeks.

sources.name: SoilGrids
sources.measures: Soil pH, texture (clay, sand, silt), organic carbon, nitrogen and cation exchange capacity by depth.
sources.limitations: Predicted by a model from soil samples and environmental data, not measured in the field. A soil test is more accurate.

sources.name: AAFC Annual Crop Inventory
sources.measures: Which crop was grown, mapped from satellite images each year since 2009.
sources.limitations: Classification can be wrong for small, mixed or unusual crops; the farmer's own records are more reliable.

sources.name: AAFC Soil Landscapes of Canada and Canada Land Inventory
sources.measures: Land capability class, dominant drainage, and agri-environmental indicators such as erosion risk, soil organic carbon change and residual nitrogen.
sources.limitations: Describes the dominant soils of an area; a single field can be quite different.

sources.name: Global crop calendar
sources.provider: Global gridded crop calendar (see the response's citation)
sources.measures: Usual planting and maturity dates for major crops.
sources.limitations: Typical regional dates, not this farm's practice or this year's conditions.

sources.name: Environment and Climate Change Canada seasonal outlook
sources.measures: Chances of above-, near- or below-normal temperature and precipitation for coming seasons.
sources.limitations: Probabilities, not forecasts of specific weather; skill is modest, especially for precipitation.

sources.name: Statistics Canada field crop yields and farm prices
sources.measures: Average yield per hectare and farm product prices by province.
sources.limitations: Provincial averages, before costs. Local prices, contracts and yields differ.

sources.name: FAO ECOCROP
sources.provider: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.measures: Each crop's optimal and tolerated pH, temperature, rainfall, cycle length, soil texture and drainage.
sources.resolution: Per crop species, not per variety.
sources.limitations: Global species ranges; modern varieties may tolerate more or less than listed.

sources.name: This app's crop estimates
sources.measures: Nitrogen fixed and needed, residue, months of ground cover, net margin and disease susceptibility per crop.
sources.limitations: Illustrative placeholders chosen to be plausible for southern Ontario. Not sourced; need agronomist review.
